summary: Generates static S-curve channels with selectable curve type, length, range mapping, and channel-extension behavior.
key_concepts: S Curve CHOP generates S-curve channels rather than transforming a required input signal.
Curve Type selects half-cosine, logistic, or arctangent curve families.
Length sets the number of samples, while Prepend and Append add samples before or after the curve.
Steepness, Linearize, and Bias shape the curve profile before it is remapped.
From Range maps input index space and To Range maps the generated curve output values.
Channel Names can generate multiple channels by pattern, and the Channel page controls sample rate and left/right extension behavior.

key_params.name: type
key_params.note: Half cosine, logistic, or arctangent curve

key_params.name: prepend
key_params.note: Samples to add before the curve

key_params.name: append
key_params.note: Samples to add after the curve

key_params.name: bias
key_params.note: Move curve bias backward or forward

key_params.name: defval
key_params.note: Default value for default-value extend mode

common_gotchas: This is a generator; it does not require an input CHOP.
Length, Prepend, and Append control sample count, not seconds unless interpreted through the sample rate.
Use Extend Left/Right deliberately when generated curves feed lookup or timeline systems.
Half cosine, logistic, and arctangent have different endpoint feel; choose by animation profile, not just smoothness.
For live one-shot easing from triggers, Timer CHOP or Phaser CHOP may be a better fit.
Linearize reduces curvature; it is not the same control as the output To Range.
Channel-name patterns can create many channels, so downstream scope assumptions should stay explicit.
